args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
COUNTERPARTY PAPER — MARKUP CONFORMITY REVIEW

Prepared by: Contracts Practice Group
Re: Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement against Firm Playbook, Executed Credit Agreement, Depository Bank Standard Form, Account Details, and Related Materials
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper

NOTE ON REDLINE CONVENTIONS: [Strike-Through] indicates deletion from the counterparty markup; **Bold Underline** indicates insertion required to conform to the firm playbook, executed credit agreement, depository bank standard form, and applicable schedules/exhibits. All changes reference the base contracts materials, schedules and exhibits, and controlling partner correspondence.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Basket" (Indemnification Threshold). 

**Redline:**
[The counterparty converted the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, pursuant to which the indemnifying party's liability attaches only once aggregate losses exceed the basket amount, and thereafter the indemnifying party is responsible only for losses in excess of the basket (not the full amount of losses from the first dollar).]

**Proposed revision (conformed to controlling instruction):**
The definition of "Indemnification Basket" shall be **reinstated as a deductible basket**, pursuant to which, once the aggregate amount of indemnifiable losses exceeds the Basket Threshold, the indemnifying party shall be liable for **the full amount of all such losses from the first dollar**; **provided, that** notwithstanding the foregoing, the client has agreed to **concede the counterparty's conversion to a tipping basket** structure, and accordingly the definition shall be conformed to reflect that the indemnifying party shall be liable only for the amount of losses in excess of the Basket Threshold; **provided, further**, that this concession is **expressly contingent upon and without prejudice to** the client's position on all other outstanding deviations, which the client has not agreed to concede.

*Cross-reference: Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities). The schedules identify retained liabilities of the counterparty. Any indemnification structure — whether deductible or tipping — must be reconciled with Schedule 5.2 to ensure that liabilities disclosed therein are not silently shifted to the client. The conceded tipping basket structure applies only to losses arising from matters NOT disclosed on Schedule 5.2.*

1.2 "Material Adverse Effect."

**Redline:**
[The counterparty adds carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter to the definition of Material Adverse Effect.]

**Proposed revision:**
"Material Adverse Effect" shall mean any event, change, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, or results of operations of the account holder; **excluding, however, any adverse effect caused by or arising from**: (i) general economic or market conditions; (ii) changes in applicable laws or regulations; **provided, that** **the exclusion in clause (ii) shall not apply to** any pending or threatened regulatory inquiry, investigation, or enforcement action (including, without limitation, the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7), **which shall be deemed a Material Adverse Effect for all purposes of this Agreement**.

*Cross-reference: Schedule 3.7 (Regulatory Inquiries). Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The counterparty's requested carve-out for "regulatory action" is overbroad and would exclude the very kind of regulatory exposure that is the subject of the disclosed inquiries. The carve-out must be narrowed to exclude only general regulatory changes, not account-specific or entity-specific regulatory actions.*

1.3 "Survival Period" / Limitation of Representations.

**Redline:**
[The counterparty introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations (including representations as to regulatory compliance, financial condition, and existence) from six (6) years to eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date.]

**Proposed revision:**
The representations and warranties of each party set forth in **Section 3.1 (Organization), Section 3.3 (Authorization), Section 3.4 (No Conflicts), Section 3.5 (Financial Statements), Section 3.6 (No Litigation), Section 3.7 (Regulatory Compliance)** shall survive the Closing Date for a period of **six (6) years** following the Closing Date, consistent with **Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)** of the base materials. All other representations and warranties shall survive for the following periods, each as set forth in Exhibit B: [insert specific survival periods as reflected in the executed credit agreement]. Under no circumstances shall the core representations (as defined in Exhibit B) have a survival period shorter than the periods set forth therein.

*Cross-reference: Exhibit B (Survival Matrix). The counterparty's proposed eighteen-month survival limitation for core representations directly contradicts Exhibit B, which establishes that core representations survive for a period of six (6) years. The client treats any reduction in the survival period for core representations as a walk-away (deal-breaker) issue.*

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 2 — INDENNIFICATION

2.1 Indemnification Cap.

**Redline:**
[The counterparty has silently reduced the aggregate indemnification cap for breaches of representations and warranties from an amount equal to the total amount of the consideration paid under the underlying credit agreement to [♦] (a material reduction).]

**Proposed revision:**
The aggregate liability of the indemnifying party for indemnification claims under this Section shall not exceed **an amount equal to the total cash consideration paid** under the underlying credit agreement; **provided, that** the foregoing cap **shall not apply to** (i) breaches of the core representations set forth in Section 3 (other than breach of Section 3.2 (Books and Records)), (ii) fraud, willful misconduct, or intentional misrepresentation, or (iii) any amounts arising from the retained liabilities disclosed on Schedule 5.2. The exclusion for retained liabilities from the cap shall ensure that Schedule 5.2 amounts are not silently shifted or capped.

*Cross-reference: Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities). The schedules identify retained liabilities of the counterparty. The cap reduction would operate to limit the maximum recovery for breaches that implicate these retained liabilities. The cap must be structured to exclude amounts attributable to retained liabilities, ensuring the client's full recovery exposure is preserved.*

2.2 Basket Structure (deductible vs. tipping).

**Redline:**
[Counterparty converted the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.]

**Proposed revision (per controlling partner instruction):**
The client **concedes the conversion** of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. This concession is made **without prejudice** to the client's right to assert all other uncorrected deviations. The parties shall retain the basket threshold as set forth in the base materials.

*Cross-reference: Deal correspondence (latest message controls). The client will concede the basket conversion. The deliverable reflects this concession and must not treat it as an outstanding issue.*

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 3 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

3.1 MAE Definition and Regulatory Carve-outs (Section 1.1 above).

**Redline:**
[The counterparty's MAE carve-out for "regulatory action" must be narrowed to exclude the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.]

**Proposed revision:**
As set forth in Section 1.2 above, insert **limitation qualifier** into the MAE definition providing that regulatory carve-outs shall not exclude **any regulatory inquiry, investigation, or enforcement action that (a) is pending or threatened as of the Closing Date, or (b) arises from facts or circumstances disclosed on Schedule 3.7**, regardless of whether such action is disclosed in the schedules.

3.2 Pending Regulatory Inquiries (Schedule 3.7).

**Redline:**
**New representation to be added:** The account holder shall represent that, except as set forth on **Schedule 3.7**, there are no pending or threatened regulatory inquiries, investigations, or enforcement actions, and to the account holder's knowledge, no facts or circumstances exist that would reasonably be expected to give rise to any such inquiry, investigation, or enforcement action.

*Cross-reference: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The base materials require that these be specifically represented and disclosed.*

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 4 — SURVIVAL AND LIMITATION PERIOD

4.1 Survival Period for Core Representations.

**Redline:**
[The counterparty's eighteen-month limitation period for core representations is rejected. Exhibit B establishes a six-year survival period for core representations.]

**Proposed revision:**
The survival period for the core representations shall be **six (6) years** from the Closing Date, as set forth in **Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)**. This provision is a **walk-away issue**; the client will not proceed with the transaction if the survival period for core representations is reduced below the periods set forth in Exhibit B.

*Cross-reference: Exhibit B (Survival Matrix). The base materials establish the survival matrix in Exhibit B. The counterparty's proposed limitation period shortens survival for core representations in direct contradiction to Exhibit B. Per the latest deal correspondence, this is a walk-away issue.*

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 5 — CONFORMITY WITH DEPOSITORY BANK STANDARD FORM

5.1 The drafter has reviewed the counterparty markup against the depository bank's standard form. To the extent the counterparty markup departs from the bank standard form regarding control, dominion, "springing" control, notification of adverse claims, and entitlement orders, such departures must be reconciled and conformed to the depository bank's standard form as implemented in the executed credit agreement. Any deviation from the approved bank form not otherwise identified in this redline shall be flagged for further review.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SUMMARY OF REDLINE CHANGES

| # | Section | Counterparty Position | Required Revision | Priority |
|---|---------|----------------------|-------------------|----------|
| 1 | §1.1 / 2.2 | Basket converted from deductible to tipping | **CONCEDE** per partner instruction — no further action | Conceded |
| 2 | §1.2 / 3.1 | MAE carve-out for regulatory action added | Narrow carve-out to exclude Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries | High |
| 3 | §2.1 | Indemnification cap silently reduced | Restore cap to full consideration amount; preserve Schedule 5.2 excl | High |
| 4 | §4.1 | Survival period for core reps shortened to 18 months | Reject; restore six-year survival per Exhibit B | Critical / Walk-away |
| 5 | §3.2 | No new rep for regulatory inquiries | Add representation for Schedule 3.7 inquiries | High |
| 6 | §5 | Potential departures from bank standard form | Conform to depository bank standard form | Verify |

END OF REDLINE

Prepared without reliance on the unrelated correspondence in administrative file 6, which was misfiled into the matter folder and does not pertain to this engagement.

args.body:
CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED
ISSUES/RISK MEMORANDUM

RE: Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviation Analysis, Risk Assessment, and Recommended Positions
MATTER: Contracts Work — Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
PREPARED FOR: Deal Team
PREPARED BY: Contracts Practice Group

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This memorandum analyzes the counterparty's markup of the Account Control Agreement against the firm's internal contracting playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, the account details, and related correspondence and checklists. The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three categories of deviations that must be identified and reconciled:

1. **Indemnification Changes**: The counterparty has (i) silently reduced the aggregate indemnification cap and (ii) converted the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Per the controlling partner instruction (latest correspondence in the matter thread), the client **concedes the basket conversion** but the cap reduction remains an outstanding issue that must be restored.

2. **Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition**: The counterparty has added carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these proposed carve-outs, making this a heightened-risk deviation that must be corrected.

3. **Survival/Limitation Period**: The counterparty has introduced a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations. Per the controlling partner instruction, **any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue** — the client will not proceed if the survival period for core representations is reduced below the matrix set forth in Exhibit B of the base materials.

The analysis below identifies each deviation in detail, referencing the applicable sections, playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, and recommended positions. The summary deviation matrix at Section V consolidates all findings.

II. MATERIALS REVIEWED

A. **Base Materials**
   1. Firm Contracting Playbook for Account Control Agreements
   2. Executed Credit Agreement (underlying facility)
   3. Depository Bank Standard Form Account Control Agreement
   4. Account Details for the subject deposit account(s)
   5. Related correspondence and closing checklists

B. **Counterparty Markup** (the "Draft ACA")
   The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces deviations analyzed below.

C. **Schedules and Exhibits**
   1. **Schedule 3.7** — discloses **two pending regulatory inquiries** that intersect the counterparty's MAE carve-outs.
   2. **Schedule 5.2** — lists retained liabilities of the counterparty that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift to the client.
   3. **Exhibit B** — sets the **survival matrix** that the counterparty's limitation-period change contradicts.

D. **Deal Team Correspondence**
   The latest message in the partner email thread **REVISES** the analysis priorities: the client **will concede the basket conversion** but the client treats **any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue**. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are **superseded** and do not control.

E. **Excluded Materials**
   Administrative file document (unrelated correspondence) was misfiled into the matter folder and has been excluded from this analysis, as it concerns a different client engagement.

III. DEVIATION ANALYSIS AND RISK ASSESSMENT

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 1: Indemnification Cap — Silent Reduction**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 8 (Indemnification); Section 1 (Definitions)

**Counterparty Markup:** The counterparty has **silently reduced** the aggregate indemnification cap. The base materials (executed credit agreement and playbook) establish an indemnification cap equal to the total cash consideration paid under the underlying credit agreement. The counterparty's markup reduces the cap to a materially lower amount.

**Playbook Requirement:** The firm playbook requires that the indemnification cap for breaches of representations and warranties be set at an amount equal to the total consideration paid under the underlying credit facility. The cap should not be reduced unless explicitly negotiated and justified by specific risk factors.

**Risk Rating: HIGH**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- The cap reduction directly limits the client's recovery for breaches of representations and warranties in the account control context.
- **Schedule 5.2** lists retained liabilities. If the cap applies to claims arising from these retained liabilities, the client would bear the risk of liabilities it specifically negotiated to be the counterparty's responsibility. The markup's cap reduction interacts with Schedule 5.2 to silently shift these retained liabilities to the client.
- In a deposit account control arrangement, the primary risk is unauthorized transfers or the counterparty's failure to honor control instructions. A reduced cap could cap recovery for such events at an amount below the value of the subject account or below the exposure from retained liabilities.

**Recommended Position:**
- **REJECT the cap reduction.** Require the cap be restored to the full consideration amount.
- Ensure that any cap **expressly excludes** amounts arising from the retained liabilities disclosed on Schedule 5.2.
- The cap should also not apply to fraud, willful misconduct, or intentional misrepresentation, consistent with the base materials.

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 2: Indemnification Basket — Deductible Converted to Tipping Basket**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 8 (Indemnification); Section 1 (Definitions)

**Counterparty Markup:** The counterparty converted the indemnification basket from a **deductible** to a **tipping** basket. Under a deductible basket, once losses exceed the basket threshold, the indemnifying party is liable for the **entire amount** of losses from the first dollar. Under a tipping basket, once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnifying party is liable only for losses **in excess of** the threshold.

**Playbook Requirement:** The firm playbook requires a deductible basket structure for indemnification claims in banking/credit transactions. This structure is consistent with market practice for secured credit arrangements.

**Risk Rating: MEDIUM (conceded per controlling instruction)**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- The conversion from deductible to tipping basket reduces the aggregate exposure of the counterparty (indemnifying party) by the amount of the basket (typically between 0.5% and 1.0% of transaction value).
- The client's potential recovery for small but repeated breaches is reduced.
- The interaction with Schedule 5.2 is material: if retained liabilities are below or just above the basket threshold, the tipping basket structure could effectively eliminate the counterparty's obligation to cover losses up to the basket amount from these liabilities.

**Recommended Position (per controlling partner instruction):**
- **CONCEDE the basket conversion** per the latest partner correspondence. The client has agreed to accept the tipping basket structure.
- This concession is made **without prejudice** to the client's rights on all other outstanding deviations.
- Ensure the concession is documented in the final agreement as expressly limited to the basket structure question and does not waive any other indemnification position.

Note: Earlier partner correspondence stated the opposite priority ordering. Per the latest controlling message, the client concedes the basket conversion. The earlier messages are superseded.

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 3: Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition — Regulatory Action Carve-outs**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 1.1 (Definitions — "Material Adverse Effect"); Sections 4 and 6 (Conditions to Closing and Covenants)

**Counterparty Markup:** The counterparty adds carve-outs to the definition of MAE for **regulatory action** of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

**Playbook Requirement:** The firm playbook requires that the MAE definition include carve-outs only for general, systemic, and non-entity-specific events (e.g., general economic conditions, general changes in law, war, terrorism). Carve-outs should NOT exclude **entity-specific** regulatory actions, investigations, or enforcement proceedings.

**Risk Rating: HIGH**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- **Schedule 3.7** discloses **two pending regulatory inquiries**. The proposed carve-out for "regulatory action" would exclude these very inquiries from the MAE definition.
- If adopted, the counterparty could claim that a material adverse development arising from either pending inquiry does not constitute an MAE, defeating the purpose of the MAE condition and the regulatory compliance representations.
- In the context of an Account Control Agreement, an MAE definition governs whether the secured party can exercise its rights to control the account upon the occurrence of certain events. An overbroad regulatory carve-out could enable the counterparty to frustrate the secured party's rights based on regulatory developments that are entity-specific.
- The interplay between the MAE carve-out and the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 is particularly acute: the carve-out appears designed to shield the counterparty from the consequences of the very regulatory exposure that is the subject of the disclosed inquiries.

**Recommended Position:**
- **REJECT the regulatory carve-out** as drafted.
- Narrow the carve-out so that it applies only to **general** changes in laws or regulations affecting businesses generally, and does **not** apply to: (i) any pending or threatened regulatory inquiry, investigation, or enforcement action; or (ii) any regulatory action arising from facts or circumstances disclosed on **Schedule 3.7**.
- Confirm that **Schedule 3.7** expressly identifies the two pending regulatory inquiries, ensuring these are not excluded from the MAE analysis.
- Add a representation in Section 3 addressing the Schedule 3.7 inquiries (see Deviation 5).

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 4: Survival/Limitation Period — Reduction for Core Representations**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 9 (Survival and Limitation); Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)

**Counterparty Markup:** The counterparty introduces a **new limitation period** that **shortens the survival** of the core representations.

**Playbook Requirement:** **Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)** of the base materials establishes the survival periods for each category of representations and warranties. The core representations (including organization, authorization, no conflicts, financial statements, no litigation, and regulatory compliance) survive for **six (6) years** following the Closing Date under the survival matrix.

**Risk Rating: CRITICAL — WALK-AWAY**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- The counterparty's proposed limitation period directly **contradicts Exhibit B**. The proposed reduction would materially shorten the period during which the client could assert claims for breach of core representations.
- In the Account Control Agreement context, the core representations include representations as to the enforceability of the control arrangement, regulatory compliance, the authority of the account holder, and the accuracy of account information — all of which may not surface for years after closing.
- Shortening the survival period disproportionately benefits the counterparty (the party providing the representations) by limiting the window for representation breach claims.
- Per the **latest controlling partner correspondence**, the client treats **any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue**. This applies regardless of the magnitude of the reduction.
- The scheduled survival matrix (Exhibit B) was expressly negotiated in the base contracts materials, and the counterparty's markup contradicts it in a material respect.

**Recommended Position:**
- **REJECT** any reduction in the survival period for core representations.
- The survival periods must conform **fully** to **Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)**.
- This is a **walk-away (deal-breaker) issue**. The client is not prepared to proceed with the transaction if the survival period for core representations is reduced below the Exhibit B matrix.
- No counteroffer should be made on this point; the client's position is absolute per the partner instruction.

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 5: Missing Representation — Pending Regulatory Inquiries**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 3 (Representations and Warranties); Schedule 3.7

**Counterparty Markup:** The counterparty's markup **fails to include** an express representation concerning pending or threatened regulatory inquiries, despite the disclosure in **Schedule 3.7** of two pending regulatory inquiries.

**Playbook Requirement:** The firm playbook requires a representation that, except as set forth on the schedules (including Schedule 3.7), there are no pending or threatened regulatory inquiries, investigations, or enforcement actions, and that to the account holder's knowledge, no facts or circumstances exist that would reasonably be expected to give rise to any such inquiry, investigation, or enforcement action.

**Risk Rating: HIGH**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- The absence of a regulatory inquiry representation means the client has no direct contractual basis for a claim if the outcome of either pending inquiry is materially adverse.
- The representation interacts with the MAE definition (Deviation 3): even if the MAE carve-out is narrowed, without an independent representation, the client's remedies are limited to termination/control rights rather than an indemnification claim.
- **Schedule 3.7** discloses the inquiries, meaning the counterparty is aware of them. A carve-out in the MAE definition combined with the absence of a specific representation would effectively immunize the counterparty from liability for the consequences of these inquiries.

**Recommended Position:**
- **ADD** an express representation (new Section 3.__) addressing pending and threatened regulatory inquiries, specifically referencing Schedule 3.7.
- Ensure the representation covers both pending/threatened inquiries as of Closing and circumstances that would reasonably be expected to give rise to such inquiries.

----------------------------------------
**DEVIATION 6: Retained Liabilities — Schedule 5.2 Interaction with Indemnification Changes**
----------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Draft ACA, Section 8 (Indemnification); Schedule 5.2

**Counterparty Markup:** The combination of the reduced indemnification cap (Deviation 1) and the tipping basket conversion (Deviation 2) **silently shifts** the retained liabilities disclosed on **Schedule 5.2** from the counterparty to the client.

**Playbook Requirement:** The firm playbook requires that retained liabilities disclosed on the schedules be expressly excluded from any indemnification cap and basket applicability. The client must not bear economic responsibility for liabilities the counterparty has agreed to retain.

**Risk Rating: HIGH**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- **Schedule 5.2** lists retained liabilities. These are obligations the counterparty has contractually agreed to bear.
- The cap reduction could limit the client's recovery for losses arising from these retained liabilities, effectively shifting them to the client despite the schedule.
- The tipping basket conversion means that even if the cap is restored, losses attributable to Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities could be excluded from recovery if they fall below the basket threshold.
- This interaction creates a **silent shift** of financial responsibility — the counterparty gets the benefit of both the reduced cap and the tipping basket, while the client carries the risk of the retained liabilities.

**Recommended Position:**
- Require that losses arising from **Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities** be: (i) **excluded from the indemnification cap**; and (ii) **excluded from the basket threshold** (i.e., such losses are recoverable from the first dollar regardless of basket application or cap).
- If the cap reduction is rejected and the cap restored per the base materials, and the basket concession applies in a structurally neutral manner, this deviation may be adequately addressed. However, express language excluding Schedule 5.2 liabilities from both cap and basket is recommended.

IV. OTHER AREAS OF REVIEW

A. **Depository Bank Standard Form Conformity**
   The markup was reviewed against the depository bank's standard form Account Control Agreement. To the extent the counterparty markup departs from the bank standard form regarding control mechanics (including dominion, "springing" control, notification of adverse claims, and entitlement orders), such departures must be reconciled and conformed to the approved bank form. Any uncorrected deviations from the bank form that affect the perfection of the secured party's security interest under UCC Article 9 should be flagged for immediate attention.

B. **Reconciliation With Executed Credit Agreement**
   The Account Control Agreement must be reconciled against the executed credit agreement to ensure consistency regarding: (i) definitions (including MAE), (ii) indemnification provisions, (iii) survival periods, and (iv) events of default and remedies. The counterparty's markup must be tested against these requirements to ensure no inconsistencies or conflicts arise.

C. **Account Details and Closing Checklists**
   The account details and closing checklists have been reviewed to ensure the ACA covers all subject accounts and that all required schedules and exhibits are properly completed. No deviations from the account details or closing checklists were identified in the counterparty markup, but the final agreement should be verified against these materials prior to execution.

D. **Excluded Misfiled Materials**
   The administrative correspondence misfiled into the matter folder has been excluded from this analysis. This document concerns a different client engagement and MUST NOT be relied upon for any purpose in this matter.
